05-00-00-910-802Airworthiness Limitation PrecautionsPDF p. 65

1. Airworthiness Limitation Precautions

A. General

(1) Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs) (a) All occurrences of CDCCLs found in this chapter of the AMM are identified by this note after each applicable CDCCL design feature: 1) NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the task: Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 05-00-00-910-802, for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs). (b) Design features that are CDCCLs are defined and controlled by Special Federal Aviation Regulation (SFAR) 88, and can be found in Section 9 of the Maintenance Planning Data (MPD) document. CDCCLs are a means of identifying certain design configuration features intended to preclude a fuel tank ignition source for the operational life of the airplane. CDCCLs are mandatory and cannot be changed or deleted without the approval of the FAA Oversight Office that is responsible for the airplane model Type Certificate. A critical fuel tank ignition source prevention feature may exist in the fuel system and its related installation or in systems that, if a failure condition were to develop, could interact with the fuel system in such a way that an unsafe condition would develop without this limitation. Strict adherence to configuration, methods, techniques, and practices as prescribed is required to ensure the CDCCL is complied with. Any use of parts, methods, techniques or practices not contained in the applicable CDCCL must be approved by the FAA Oversight Office that is responsible for the airplane model Type Certificate. (2) Airworthiness Limitation Instructions (ALIs) (a) All occurrences of fuel tank system ALIs found in this chapter of the AMM are identified by this note after each applicable ALI inspection feature: 1) NOTE ALI - Refer to the task: Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 05-00-00-910-802, for important information on airworthiness limitation instructions (ALIs). (b) Inspection features that are ALIs are defined and controlled by Special Federal Aviation Regulation (SFAR) 88, and can be found in Section 9 of the Maintenance Planning Data (MPD) document. These ALIs identify inspection features related to fuel tank ignition source prevention which must be done to maintain the design level of safety for the operational life of the airplane. These inspection features are mandatory and cannot be changed or deleted without the approval of the FAA Oversight Office that is responsible for the airplane model Type Certificate. Strict adherence to methods, techniques and practices as prescribed is required to ensure the ALI is complied with. Any use of methods, techniques or practices not contained in these ALIs must be approved by the FAA Oversight Office that is responsible for the airplane model Type Certificate.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 100 Lower Half of Fuselage 200 Upper Half of Fuselage 500 Left Wing 600 Right Wing EFFECTIVITY ALL

C. Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs)

(1) Make sure you follow the procedures for items identified as CDCCLs.

(1) Make sure you follow the procedures for items identified as ALIs.

05-00-00-910-804Enhanced Zonal Inspection Program (EZAP) PrecautionsPDF p. 66

2. Enhanced Zonal Inspection Program (EZAP) Precautions

A. General

(1) Enhanced Zonal Analysis Procedure (EZAP) and associated Electrical Wiring Interconnection System (EWIS) (a) Enhanced Zonal Analysis Procedure (EZAP) is an analytical procedure required by Part 25, Appendix H, Section H25.5(a)(1) that identifies the physical and environmental conditions contained in each zone of an airplane, analyzes the effects of these conditions on electrical wiring and components, and assesses the possibilities for smoke and fire. The end result of the analysis are inspection and restoration tasks in the form of EWIS ICA. (b) Electrical Wiring Interconnection System (EWIS): means any wire, power feeder, wiring device, or combination of these, including termination devices, installed in any area of the airplane for the purpose of transmitting electrical energy, including data and signals, between two or more intended termination points. EWIS is defined in full by 14 CFR section 25.1701. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) The Zonal Inspection Program includes a general visual and, if required, physical check of the general condition and security of attachment of the accessible systems and structures items contained in defined zones. This includes checks for degradation such as chafing of tubing, loose duct supports, damage to wiring and connected EWIS, cable and pulley wear, fluid leaks, electrical bonding, general condition of fasteners, inadequate drainage, etc., and general corrosion, not covered in the MSG-3 analysis. The zonal inspection is not intended as a quality assurance after maintenance check for determining proper reassembly of systems, components, structures, or powerplants. The zonal program packages a number of General Visual (GV) Inspections into one or more zonal inspections. The program includes any GV inspection tasks required to assure security of attachment and general condition of any system or structural items within the zone. (2) Equivalent Tools, Fixtures, Test Equipment, and Consumable Materials (a) When the procedures in this manual identify tools, equipment, and consumable materials, you can use equivalent alternatives. If you use alternative tools, equipment, or consumable materials, make sure that they give the same results and are as safe to the parts and personnel as the tools, equipment, or consumable materials specified in the procedure.

B. References

Reference Title 20-60-07-913-801 Protection of the EWIS During Maintenance (P/B 201)

C. Protection of EWIS During Maintenance, Repair and Alterations

SUBTASK 05-00-00-910-006 WARNING OBEY THE MANUFACTURER'S PROCEDURES WHEN YOU DO EZAP MAINTENANCE, OR MAINTENANCE THAT HAS AN EFFECT ON EWIS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE PROCEDURES, IT CAN INCREASE THE RISK OF AN IGNITION SOURCE FOR FIRES. INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) Make sure you follow the procedures for items identified as EZAP. (2) Refer to Protection of the EWIS During Maintenance, TASK 20-60-07-913-801.

C. Nose Landing Gear and Forward Fuselage Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-040 (1) Perform the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) and forward fuselage inspection procedure as stated in PAGEBLOCK 05-51-37/201, if it was a “Hard Nose Gear Landing”, or a “High Drag or High Side Load Condition”.

D. Main Landing Gear Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-041 (1) Examine the Main Landing Gear (MLG) areas as follows (Figure 203, Figure 204): (a) The tires for damage (TASK 32-45-00-700-803). (b) The wheels for damage; cracks, missing tie-bolts, heat shield (TASK 32-45-00-700-801). (c) The shock struts at the top and bottom end for signs of fluid leakage. NOTE: A small quantity of hydraulic fluid on the inner cylinder is satisfactory. (d) The top end of the shock strut for cracks and bolt distortion. (e) The outer door and linkage. (f) The center door and linkage. (g) The inner door and linkage. (h) The trunnions and shock strut top end, including bushing edges/flanges and visible pin's external surface plating. (i) The side strut and trunnion attach fittings of the main landing gear. (j) The landing gear walking beam to wing structure attachment fittings. (k) The landing gear trunnion to landing gear walking beam attachment and landing gear trunnion to wing structure. (l) The landing gear beam. (m) The main landing beam outboard support fitting. (n) The forward trunnion support fitting. (o) The main landing gear beam inboard support (hanger link fitting). (p) If the airplane departs the prepared surface, do the inspections outlined in Phase IB.

E. Fuselage, Wing, Empennage and Engine Strut/Nacelle Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-042 (1) Examine the fuselage areas that follow: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Examine the upper and lower fuselage skin panels forward and aft of the wing. NOTE: Permanent wrinkles frequently occur on the lower side of the fuselage skins aft of STA 727. (b) If you found wrinkles on the skin panels and you did not know they were there before, make an internal inspection. NOTE: If the wrinkles were there before, make a careful inspection of the wrinkles for cracks. (c) Examine the keel beam chords, stiffeners, webs and splices at station 663 thru 727A. SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-056 (2) Perform a general visual examination of the areas around the probes and static ports. (a) If obvious visual damage is found, do an RVSM check: SRM 51-10-03. (3) Examine the wing lower surface leading edge, inspar, and trailing edge for signs of damage.

F. Cabin Inspections

NOTE: If inspections of the forward cabin were already performed during Phase I Inspection, TASK 05-51-37-200-806, then they do not need to be repeated. SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-043 (1) Do the following cabin inspections that follow to find possible damage: (a) Do a visual inspection of all ceiling panels (and video monitors, if applicable) for dislodging and evidence due to impact damage. (b) Do a visual inspection of all overhead bins for evidence of looseness and impact damage. (2) If any cabin damage was found in the Phase IA Cabin Inspections including the ceiling panels, overhead bins, or the video monitors then continue the Cabin Inspection in Phase IB and Phase II. If no damage was found, no further cabin inspections are required, and it is not necessary to continue the cabin inspections in Phase IB and Phase II.

E. Main Landing Gear Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-044 (1) Examine the main landing gear areas as follows: (a) Examine the tires for damage (Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803) (b) Examine the wheels for damage; cracks, missing tie-bolts, heat shield (Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801) (c) Examine the brake assemblies for damage (Main Landing Gear Brake Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-41-41-700-802) (d) The shock strut of the main gear for fluid leakage (top & bottom) (e) The doors and linkages of the main gear strut (f) The landing gear beam and attachment fittings (g) Remove the forward trunnion fuse pin [5] and perform a detailed visual inspection if any of the following events occurred such that a significant drag loading on the main gear is expected: 1) The main landing gear hit an obstacle of large mass, or 2) The aircraft landed short of the prepared surface, or EFFECTIVITY ALL 3) The airplane ran off the prepared surface which produced a peak deceleration that was more severe than maximum effort braking. NOTE: Inspection of the forward trunnion fuse pins may be deferred for non-revenue ferry flights only. SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-074 (2) If the airplane departs off the prepared surface, do the following: (a) Examine the tires for damage (Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803) (b) Examine the wheels for damage; cracks, missing tiebolts, heat shield (Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801) 1) After the examination, if the tires and wheels have not been damaged, do these steps: a) Do the recovery and/or movement of the airplane to the prepared surface. 2) If the wheel heat shield(s) is/are bent and prevents the free rotation of the wheel and the tire assembly that contacts the brake: a) Bend the heat shield(s) to allow free rotation of the wheel and tire assembly. NOTE: The airplane can be towed to a location where further inspections and examinations will be performed. 3) After the examination, if the tires and wheels are determined to be damaged and prevents the recovery and/or movement of the airplane to the prepared surface, do these steps: a) Replace the wheel and tire assemblies to allow recovery and movement of the airplane (MAIN LANDING GEAR WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 32-45-11/401). 4) Examine the brake assemblies for damage (Main Landing Gear Brake Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-41-41-700-802) a) If a brake assembly is damaged and does not allow the rotation of the wheel and tire assembly, do these steps: NOTE: If the wheel and tire assembly cannot rotate because the brake assembly is damaged, the brake assembly must be removed. After the brake assembly is removed and the wheel and tire assembly is installed, then the airplane can be towed safely. <1> Remove the Wheel and Tire assembly (Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Removal, TASK 32-45-11-000-801). <2> Remove the brake assembly (Main Landing Gear Brake Removal, TASK 32-41-41-000-801). <3> Install the Wheel and Tire assembly (Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Installation, TASK 32-45-11-400-801). NOTE: The wheel and tire assembly is installed to allow the airplane to be recovered. 5) After the airplane has been moved to a location for further examination, and before next flight, do these steps: a) Replace the damaged wheel and tire assemblies (MAIN LANDING GEAR WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 32-45-11/401) EFFECTIVITY ALL <1> If the wheel and tire assemblies were replaced before the airplane recovery. Clean the wheel and tire assemblies of unwanted material. <2> After the wheel and tire assemblies have been cleaned, examine the wheels and tires for damage (Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803, Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801). <3> If no damage is found, the wheels and tires are serviceable. b) Prior to flight, replace the brake assemblies (MAIN LANDING GEAR BRAKE - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 32-41-41/401). c) Remove the brake sleeves and examine the axles. NOTE: There are occasions where the airplane lands and one Main Landing Gear (MLG) departs the prepared surface but then returns to the prepared surface and taxis to the gate. In this case, the wheel/tire￾and brake-assemblies need to be cleaned of any debris and examined. SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-075 (3) During a landing, if one main landing gear departs from the prepared surface and returns to the prepared surface and taxis to the gate, do these steps: (a) Examine the tires for damage (Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803) (b) Examine the wheels for damage; cracks, missing tiebolts, heat shield (Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801) (c) Examine the brake assemblies for damage (Main Landing Gear Brake Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-41-41-700-802)

F. Nose Landing Gear Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-045 (1) Perform the NOSE LANDING GEAR AND FORWARD FUSELAGE - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL INSPECTION), PAGEBLOCK 05-51-37/201, if it was a "Hard Nose Gear Landing", or a "High Drag or High Side Load Condition".

G. Fuselage Inspection

NOTE: If inspections of the forward fuselage were already performed during Nose Gear and Forward Fuselage NOSE LANDING GEAR AND FORWARD FUSELAGE - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL INSPECTION), PAGEBLOCK 05-51-37/201, then they do not need to be repeated. SUBTASK 05-51-01-200-003 (1) Examine the aft side of the pressure bulkhead for signs of buckling, deformation or damage. (a) Do a detailed visual inspection of the entire aft side of the BS 1016 aft pressure bulkhead. Give particular attention to the upper bulkhead structure between skin stringers S-10L and S-10R. NOTE: Access to the interior unpressurized aft pressure bulkhead area is through the aft access hatch, 311BL.

H. Wing Area Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-01-860-001 (1) Extend the Trailing Edge (TE) flaps, do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 05-51-01-860-002 (2) Extend the Leading Edge (LE) flaps and slats, do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Extension, TASK 27-81-00-860-803. SUBTASK 05-51-01-040-007 WARNING DO THE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE FOR THE TRAILING EDGE FLAP BEFORE YOU DO WORK ON THE FLAP SYSTEM. THE FLAPS MOVE QUICKLY. THEY CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (3) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801. SUBTASK 05-51-01-040-012 WARNING DO THE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE FOR THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THE FLAPS AND SLATS MOVE QUICKLY. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (4) (Preferred Configuration) If the LE flaps and slat locks are available, do these steps to secure the area under the wing for inspection: (a) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Deactivation, TASK 27-81-00-040-801. (b) Do this task: Leading Edge Flap and Slat Locks Installation, TASK 27-81-00-480-801. SUBTASK 05-51-01-040-013 WARNING DO THE ALTERNATIVE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE FOR THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THE FLAPS AND SLATS MOVE QUICKLY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (5) (Alternate Configuration) If the LE flaps and slat locks are not available, do these steps to secure the area under the wing for inspection: NOTE: This alternate method is used to secure the areas under the wing leading edge and trailing edge when no other maintenance action or structural inspection is required, scheduled or unscheduled. (a) Do these steps to secure the hydraulic system: 1) Make sure that the hydraulic power is removed (TASK 29-11-00-860-805). 2) Make sure that the HYD PUMPS A ELEC 2 and the HYD PUMPS B ELEC 1 switches are in the OFF position. 3) Make sure that the HYD PUMPS ENG switch is in the ON position. NOTE: The HYD PUMPS ENG switch should be left in the ON position. This will increase the life of the depressurization solenoid which becomes energized when the HYD PUMPS ENG switch is put in the OFF position. 4) Attach a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the HYD PUMPS switches. (b) Make sure that the Proximity Sensor Electronics Unit (PSEU) is in GROUND MODE (TASK 32-09-00-860-802). EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 7 C00210 FLIGHT CONTROL FLAP SHUTOFF VALVES (d) Make sure that the ALTERNATE FLAP ARM switch is in the OFF position. (e) Attach a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the flap control lever and the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch. (f) Do these steps to secure the LE Uncommanded Motion (UCM) shutoff valve: 1) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192BR ECS Ram Air Inlet Mixing Duct Panel - Forward 2) Remove the lockwire from the manual override lever (handle). 3) Move the manual override lever on the LE UCM shutoff valve to the OFF position. NOTE: The lever should move with very little force. If the lever is tight, you may need hydraulic pressure and the Flap/Slat Electronics Unit (FSEU) to release the pressure on the LE UCM shutoff valve. 4) Install the lockout pin, SPL-1746, in the manual override lever to keep the lever in the OFF position. a) If the tool cannot be easily installed then it is necessary to supply system B hydraulic power and then use the FSEU to relieve the pressure on the LE UCM shutoff valve. <1> Use the FSEU procedure below but replace the selection of the LE DEPR valve for the LE UCM shutoff valve. NOTE: Two persons will be necessary when the FSEU is used to operate the LE UCM shutoff valve. 5) Attach a DO-NOT-REMOVE tag on the rig pin or lockout pin, SPL-1746. (g) Do these steps to secure the LE cruise depressurization valve (located in the main landing gear wheel well): 1) If the valve has a tab, cut the tab from the valve (SB 27-1242). 2) Remove the lockwire from the manual override lever (handle). 3) Move the manual override lever up to the OFF position. NOTE: Do not force movement of the lever with tools. The lever should move with very little force. If the lever is tight, you may need hydraulic pressure and the FSEU to relieve the pressure on the LE cruise depressurization valve. a) If you cannot move the manual override lever, use the FSEU and hydraulic pressure to operate the LE cruise depressurization valve. NOTE: Two persons will be necessary when the FSEU is used to operate the LE cruise depressurization valve. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. <1> Supply system B hydraulic power (TASK 29-11-00-860-801). <2> Use the FSEU to release the pressure on the LE cruise depressurization valve, as follows: <a> Get access to the main equipment center, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door <b> Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 7 C00210 FLIGHT CONTROL FLAP SHUTOFF VALVES <c> Push the ON/OFF button. <d> EXISTING FAULTS..... press NO. <e> Press NO until OTHER FUNCTIONS. <f> OTHER FUNCTIONS..... press YES. <g> SET OUTPUTS..... press YES. <h> Press NO until LE DEPR VALVE. <i> LE DEPR VALVE..... press YES. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU MOVE THE MANUAL OVERRIDE HANDLE TO THE OFF POSITION AND INSTALL THE RIG PIN IN LESS THAN 75 SECONDS. THE FSEU WILL AUTOMATICALLY CHANGE THE POSITION OF THE VALVE AND THE OVERRIDE HANDLE AFTER 75 SECONDS. THE MANUAL OVERRIDE HANDLE CAN MOVE SUDDENLY AND CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. <j> SET ON..... press YES. <3> Move the manual override lever up to the OFF position. 4) Install the lockout pin, SPL-1746, in the manual override lever to keep the lever in the OFF position. NOTE: If the newer -1003 cruise depressurization valve is installed on the airplane then the lockout pin, SPL-1746, will stop the movement of the leading edge flaps and slats when hydraulic power is applied. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING IF A -1001 CRUISE DEPRESSURIZATION VALVE IS INSTALLED, DO NOT APPLY HYDRAULIC POWER TO EXTEND OR RETRACT THE TRAILING EDGE WHEN THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS ARE DEACTIVATED. A -1001 VALVE CAN HAVE HYDRAULIC PRESSURE LEAKAGE AND WILL NOT STOP THE MOVEMENT OF THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. MOVEMENT OF THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO AN OPEN THRUST REVERSER AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL. a) If the older -1001 cruise depressurization valve is installed on the airplane, do these steps: NOTE: A leading edge device creep condition has been associated with a “lap assembly” tolerances or a combination of “lap assembly” tolerances and the use of the smaller 0.3125 in. (7.9375 mm) diameter lockout pin, SPL-1746, that could be the cause of hydraulic pressure leakage through the older -1001 valve. <1> Make sure that the hydraulic power is turned OFF after the leading edge devices have been moved to their desired position. <2> Make sure to attach the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, to both ELEC 1 and the ELEC 2 HYD PUMP switches on the P5 panel. NOTE: Due to -1001 cruise depressurization valve installed, hydraulics cannot be operated until LE flaps and slats are re-activated. 5) Attach a DO-NOT-REMOVE tag on the rig pin or lockout pin, SPL-1746. 6) If the FSEU was used, then do the following: a) Remove system B hydraulic power (TASK 29-11-00-860-805). b) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 7 C00210 FLIGHT CONTROL FLAP SHUTOFF VALVES (h) Do these steps to prevent leading edge devices extension or retraction by the standby hydraulic system: 1) Disconnect the electrical connector from the LE standby drive shutoff valve. a) After you disconnect the electrical connector, examine the connector for corrosion. NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector(s) can be done after the removal step or before the installation step of the electrical connector. This is an operator option. b) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03). EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE MANUAL OVERRIDE LEVER IS IN POSITION 1 TO PREVENT THE MOVEMENT OF THE LEADING EDGE SLATS. IF THE LEADING EDGE SLATS MOVE, DAMAGE TO AN OPEN THRUST REVERSER AND INJURIES TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. 2) Make sure that the override lever is in the Position 1 (standby hydraulic power OFF). NOTE: If the manual override lever at the LE standby drive shutoff valve is in Position 2 and the standby hydraulic system is then pressurized, the leading edge slats will move to the full extend position. 3) Install the lockout pin, SPL-1746. NOTE: The lock, SPL-1675, can be used on the standby hydraulic system for the alternate deactivation (TASK 27-81-00-040-801). 4) Attach a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the LE standby drive shutoff valve. (i) Do the LE flaps and slats tryout (TASK 27-81-00-040-801). (j) Remove power from the airplane, do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812. (k) Make sure the BAT switch is in the OFF position. (l) Attach a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the BAT switch. SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-076 WARNING DO NOT GO INTO THE WING LEADING EDGE AND TRAILING EDGE AREAS. THESE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (6) Examine the wing area as follow: NOTE: The wing areas must be examined from the ground. Unsatisfactory conditions or descrepancies can be visually identified from a safe distance. If damage is found in the extended wing areas, then it is necessary to install the leading edge flaps and slat locks before further maintenance action. (a) Examine the extended wing trailing edges for signs of damage. (b) Examine the extended wing leading edges for signs of damage. (c) The strut-to-wing fairing panels on the upper and lower nacelle. (d) If there was a dragged engine nacelle condition that occurred, do the following: 1) Dragged Engine Nacelle/Fan Blade Out/Engine Seizure/Engine and Strut Damage Conditional Inspection, TASK 05-51-10-210-801.

D. Main Landing Gear Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-005 (1) Examine the Main Landing Gear (MLG) areas as follows (Figure 203, Figure 204). (a) Examine the outer and inner cylinder lugs. (b) Examine the trunnion fitting area of the outer cylinder including the bushing edges/flanges. (c) Examine the torsion links. (d) Examine the actuator walking beam and linkage fittings. (e) Examine the MLG beam fitting and AFT trunnion support fitting on the shock strut for cracks. EFFECTIVITY ALL (f) Examine these MLG pins and fuse pins: side strut hanger link assembly pin [1], side strut hanger link pin [2], side strut pin [3], fuse pin [4], fuse pin [5], upper hanger link pin [6], pin [7], lower hanger link pin [8], aft trunnion pin [9], and fwd trunnion pin [10]. 1) For vertical overload remove the MLG Beam outboard attachment fuse pin [4] and perform a detailed visual inspection. a) Remove the MLG (TASK 32-11-00-000-801). b) Remove the MLG support beam as required (TASK 57-15-00-000-801). c) If damage is found remove the forward trunnion fuse pins and perform a detailed visual inspection. 2) For a high drag or high side load overload, remove the forward trunnion fuse pins and perform a detailed visual inspection. a) Remove the MLG (TASK 32-11-00-000-801). b) Remove the MLG support beam as required (TASK 57-15-00-000-801). c) If damage is found remove MLG Beam outboard attachment fuse pin and perform a detailed visual inspection. (g) Make sure that the pressure and hydraulic fluid levels in the main landing gear shock struts are correct, do this task: Main Landing Gear Shock Strut Fluid Check, TASK 12-15-31-610-801. 1) If the fluid level is low; do these steps: a) Do this task: Replace the Active Seals with the Spare Seals, TASK 32-11-21-960-801. b) Remove the inner cylinder and examine it for distortions or cracks, do this task: Landing Gear Inner Cylinder Chrome Inspection, TASK 32-00-10-211-801. c) Examine the orifice support tube, while it is on the airplane, for cracks. (h) Examine the wheel well of the main landing gear for fuel or other fluid leaks. (i) If a high drag or side load condition, and a hard landing occur at the same time, remove the main gear inner cylinders, do this task: Landing Gear Inner Cylinder Chrome Inspection, TASK 32-00-10-211-801. 1) Look for distortions or cracks in the inner cylinder. (j) Examine the side strut and side strut attachments. (k) If any main landing gear wheels are removed because of a blown tire, do the steps that follow: 1) Examine the wheel structure for damage. 2) Examine the brake assembly for damage (TASK 32-41-41-700-803).

E. Nose Landing Gear Inspection

NOTE: If no damage was found in the nose landing gear inspections of NOSE LANDING GEAR AND FORWARD FUSELAGE - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL INSPECTION), PAGEBLOCK 05-51-37/201, then no further nose landing gear inspections are required. SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-025 (1) If not previously done during the inspection of Phase I Inspection, TASK 05-51-37-200-806, do the following: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Jack the nose landing gear Lift the Airplane Nose Landing Gear with the Axle Jack at Jack Point E, TASK 07-11-03-580-802 or Lift the Airplane Nose with the Nose Jack at Jack Point D, TASK 07-11-21-580-801. SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-006 (2) Examine the nose landing gear areas that follows. (a) Examine carefully the areas near the trunnion and the drag-strut support fittings. (b) Do this task: Nose Landing Gear Inspection, TASK 32-21-00-200-801. (c) Do this task: Nose Landing Gear Torsional Freeplay Inspection, TASK 32-21-00-700-801. (d) Examine the nose landing gear wheel well. (e) Examine the drag strut support fittings. (f) Examine the outer-cylinder-trunnion-fitting area and the drag brace linkage. (g) Make sure that the pressure and hydraulic fluid level in the nose landing gear shock strut is correct, do this task: Nose Landing Gear Shock Strut Servicing, Airplane on the Ground, TASK 12-15-41-610-802. 1) If the pressure and hydraulic fluid level is not correct, remove the nose landing gear inner cylinder, do this task: NLG Inner Cylinder Removal, TASK 32-21-24-000-801. a) Examine the inner cylinder for cracks and other types of damage. b) Examine the orifice support tube for distortion and cracks. (h) Examine the wheel well of the nose landing gear for buckling and other damage. 1) Make sure that there are no loose fasteners in the web of the nose wheel well near the trunnion support fittings. 2) Look for fluid leaks. (i) Do a check of the rigging of the steering mechanism. 1) Do this task: Nose Wheel Steering System Test, TASK 32-51-00-700-801. (j) Examine the axle for bends. 1) Spin the wheels. a) Make sure that there is no binding that may be caused by a bent axle. 2) Place a level on the outboard wheel rims. a) Make sure that both wheels are vertical. (k) If it was a hard nose gear landing or a high drag or side load condition, do these steps: 1) Remove the nose landing gear inner cylinder, do this task: NLG Inner Cylinder Removal, TASK 32-21-24-000-801. a) Examine the inner cylinder for damage.

F. Fuselage and Empennage Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-01-040-004 (1) Examine the fuselage as follows: (a) Examine the lower fuselage structure. 1) Look carefully at the area below the body floor beams immediately aft of the wing center section. (b) Examine the wing-to-fuselage joints and the wheel well bulkheads. (c) Examine the upper fuselage structure above the primary wing spars. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) Examine the area around leading edge dorsal fin: Number Name/Location 321A Vertical Fin, Dorsal Fin (e) Examine the external fuselage skin at BS 1016 for signs of buckling, deformation or damage. 1) Do a detailed visual inspection of the exterior fuselage skin 10 in. (25.4 cm) forward and aft of the BS 1016 skin butt joint between stringers S-10L and S-10R. NOTE: Gain access to the exterior of the fuselage skin BS 1016 under the vertical stabilizer fairing, 323AL and 323AR. (f) Examine the wheel well bulkheads of the main landing gear. (g) Examine the side-of-body ribs for cracks in the area of the rear spar. (h) Examine the rear spar for permanent buckles between the tank end and side of the body. (i) Examine the nose landing gear wheel well aft bulkhead. (j) Examine the fuselage structure immediately outboard of the nose wheel well. (k) Examine the fuselage skin attachments above the landing gear beam. (l) Look for signs of fuel leaks or other fluids leaking in the areas that follow: 1) the wing 2) the nacelles 3) the engine struts 4) the external surfaces of the fuselage 5) the nose landing gear wheel well 6) the main landing gear wheel well. (m) Examine the lower fuselage (body sections 46 and 48) for signs that it touched the runway. (n) If there are signs of damage, examine the areas that follow. NOTE: Look for broken parts, bent parts, or other types of damage. 1) the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) firewall 2) the APU drain 3) the APU doors 4) the drain mast 5) the lower fuselage skin, stringers, frames, and shears ties. SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-007 (2) Make sure that the flight controls move freely.

G. Wing Area Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-008 (1) Do an inspection of the wing areas that follow: WARNING DO NOT GO INTO THE WING LEADING EDGE AND TRAILING EDGE AREAS BEFORE YOU INSTALL SAFETY LOCKS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONNEL FROM ACCIDENTAL FLAP/SLAT OPERATION CAN OCCUR. (a) Install the leading edge flaps and slat locks. EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Do this task: Leading Edge Flap and Slat Locks Installation, TASK 27-81-00-480-801. 2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801. (b) Examine the wings and nacelles for fuel or other fluid leaks. (c) Examine the wing ribs along the aft side of the rear spar, WSTA 228.25 and 253.00 for cracks. (d) Examine the upper and lower trailing edge panels and the airplane structure for damage. 1) Make sure that you examine the area near the main landing gear beam carefully. (e) Examine the flap areas that follow for sheared rivets and structure damage: 1) The inboard and outboard trailing edge flaps 2) The flap tracks 3) The drive screws 4) The linkages and fairings. (f) Examine the inboard and outboard spoilers for sheared rivets and structure damage. (g) Examine the flap track bolts on the outboard trailing edge flap for damage that can occur if the flaps touched the ground. (h) Examine the flap track bolts on the inboard trailing edge flap for damage that can occur if the flaps touched the ground. (i) Make sure that the flight controls move freely and cable tension is satisfactory. (j) For airplanes with winglets: 1) Examine the winglet and attachment at rib 27 (WBL 658.17).

H. Do a Test of the Landing Gears

SUBTASK 05-51-01-580-002 (1) Do a check of the nose and main landing gear. NOTE: Look for signs of interference, misalignment, or distortion. (a) Lift the airplane on jacks, do these tasks: Lift the Airplane with the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-815. (b) Retract and extend the nose landing gear, do this task: Operational Test for the Nose Landing Gear, TASK 32-33-00-710-801. (c) Retract and extend the main landing gear, do this task: Main Landing Gear Operational Test, TASK 32-32-00-710-801. (d) Retract and then extend the main landing gear with the manual system to make sure they operate correctly, do this task: Main Gear Manual Extension System Test - Airplane on Jacks, TASK 32-34-00-730-801. (e) Retract and then extend the nose landing gear with the manual system to make sure it operates correctly, do this task: Nose Gear Manual Extension System Test - Airplane on Jacks, TASK 32-35-00-730-801

(f) Examine galley tie rod attachments for damage consisting of breakage, cracks, and deformation. Inspect the tie rods for evidence of buckling or rupture. 1) If any defect is found, replace as necessary. (g) Examine the galley floor fittings for damage consisting of breakage, cracks, and deformation. 1) If any defect is found, replace as necessary. (h) Examine, closet tie rod attachments for damage consisting of breakage, cracks, and deformation. 1) If any defect is found, replace as necessary. (i) Examine the closet floor fittings for damage consisting of breakage, cracks, and deformation. 1) If any defect is found, replace as necessary.

SUBTASK 05-51-01-210-009 (1) Do the steps that follow to examine the engine areas: (a) Do an engine inspection after a hard landing. 1) Do this task: Inspection Of The Engine After A Hard Landing, TASK 71-00-00-200-803-F00. 2) Examine the engine nacelle if it touched the ground. (b) If damage was found on the strut to wing fairing, then do this task: Dragged Engine Nacelle/Fan Blade Out/Engine Seizure/Engine and Strut Damage Conditional Inspection, TASK 05-51-10-210-801.

SUBTASK 05-51-01-211-005 (1) Do a check of the cargo loading system to make sure it operates correctly with the containers and pallets. (a) Look at the components that follow: 1) Make a check of the cargo restraint system in all cargo compartments. 2) Visually check the following: a) The rollers, EFFECTIVITY ALL b) The side guides, c) The seat tracks, d) The pallet locks. 3) Examine all components for breaks, cracks, and missing retaining lips. a) Make sure that the cargo loading rollers (where installed) move freely.

L. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 05-51-01-410-002 (1) Install the components you removed if they are serviceable, or install replacement parts. 2. Severe or Unusual Turbulence, Excessive Maneuver, Buffet, or Speeds More than the Design Limits Conditional Inspection

A. General

(1) When the conditional inspection tells you to "examine" a component, look for these conditions (repair or replace components, if it is necessary): (a) Cracks (b) Pulled apart structure (c) Loose paint (paint flakes) (d) Discoloration (e) Twisted parts (distortion) (f) Wrinkles or buckles in the structure (g) Bent components (h) Loose fasteners (i) Fasteners that have pulled out or are gone (j) Delaminations (k) Fiber breakouts (l) Misalignment (m) Interference (n) Nicks or gouges (o) Other signs of damage.

D. Severe or Unusual Turbulence Condition

SUBTASK 05-51-04-210-016 (1) Severe turbulence is identified as turbulence which causes large, abrupt changes in the altitude and/or attitude. The airplane could be out of control for short periods. It usually causes large variations in airspeed. Passengers and crew are moved violently against their seat belts and loose objects are moved around the airplane. SUBTASK 05-51-04-210-024 (2) An inspection is required when the aircraft has encountered severe turbulence. The pilot must report the suspected encounter of this event. If the pilot reports that the aircraft has encountered severe turbulence, refer to “Examine Airplane Structure and Wing Areas” and “Cabin Inspections” in this section.

E. Excessive Maneuver Condition

SUBTASK 05-51-04-210-018 (1) Excessive maneuvers are maneuvers that result in severe and abnormal aircraft response and/or attitude, and/or exceeding of the flight maneuvering vertical load factors, specified below. Excessive maneuvers could be due to rapid or large alternating control inputs i.e., control column, rudder pedals, and control wheel. (a) The vertical acceleration load limits shown below are directly applicable to excessive maneuvers. 1) Flaps up . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 2.5g to -1.0g 2) Flaps down . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 2.0g to 0.0g EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 05-51-04-210-025 (2) An inspection is required when the aircraft has been involved in an excessive maneuver. The pilot must report the suspected encounter of this event. If the pilot reports that the airplane has been involved in an excessive maneuver, refer to "Examine Airplane Structure and Wing Areas" and "Cabin Inspections" in this section.

F. Severe or Unusual Buffet Condition

SUBTASK 05-51-04-210-002 (1) If an unusual vibration, an unusual maneuver or a severe or unusual buffet condition occurs in-flight, do the "Examine the Airplane Structure and Wing Areas" steps in the following task: Severe or Unusual Turbulence, Excessive Maneuver, Buffet, or Speeds More than the Design Limits Conditional Inspection, TASK 05-51-04-210-801. SUBTASK 05-51-04-210-003 (2) If a stall occurs after the initial buffet or stick shaker condition, an inspection is necessary. (a) Do the Stall (After Initial Buffet or Stick Shaker) Structural Inspection Procedure.

G. Airplane Speeds More than the Design Limits

SUBTASK 05-51-04-210-004 (1) The maximum design speed of the airplane for flight operations are as follows: NOTE: The Maximum Operating Limit Speed is in Section 1, LIMITATIONS of the Airplane Flight Manual (AFM). (a) The airplane Maximum Operating Speed (VMO) is 340 knots (630 km/h) when the airplane is at or below 25,968 ft (7915 m). (b) Above 25,968 ft (7915 m), the airplane is limited to a Maximum Operating Mach (MMO) of 0.82. (c) The overspeed clacker will activate when the airplane exceeds the VMO or MMO. SUBTASK 05-51-04-210-005 (2) Do the “Examine the Airplane Structure and Wing Areas” procedure in the task if one or both conditions that follow occurs: NOTE: When the overspeed event occurs at 25,968 ft (7915 m) or below, it should be viewed in knots. Overspeed events above 25,968 ft (7915 m) should be viewed in mach. (a) The airplane speed exceeds the VMO by 20 knots (37 km/h) or more. (b) The airplane speed exceeds the MMO by 0.02 Mach or more.

05-51-07-210-801High Energy StopPDF p. 867

2. High Energy Stop

A. General

(1) The level of the inspection depends on the level of absorbed kinetic energy. (2) High energy stop is an event where the brake energy falls within the "Caution" or "Fuse Plug Melt" zones. (3) The heat absorbed by the airplane brake is slowly, but not fully transmitted to the wheel, tire, axle, and in-axle components. (4) The wheels have fuse plugs which are designed to melt and release the tire pressure. NOTE: The fuse plugs melt at a specific design temperature. (a) This is to stop ruptures of the tires and wheels when the wheel temperature gets too high. (5) If brake fire occurs, do the steps in the "High Energy Stop Condition Inspection - IN FUSE PLUG MELT range or Brake Fire" section. (6) The brake cooling time starts once the airplane is stationary and no further brake applications are performed. (7) Use the brake energy chart to approximate energy absorbed by a brake unit (Figure 202 or Figure 203). (a) This chart will give only the approximate energy absorbed during the stop. 1) The factors that follow will also affect the energy absorbed: a) The residual energy from the previous stop b) The runway slope c) The wind conditions d) The thrust reverser use. (b) Listed below are example values to show you how to use the Brake Energy Chart to obtain result values (Figure 201): NOTE: The brake temperature monitoring system (BTMS) indications are also shown in the bottom of the figure. If brake cooling is determined from the BTMS, use the hottest brake indication 10 to 15 minutes after the airplane has come to a complete stop, or in-flight with gear retracted to determine recommended cooling schedule. NOTE: The data values given below are for example only and must not be used to determine a specific airplane absorbed energy by a brake unit. The airplane operators must use actual values generated by the specific airplane high energy stop/heat event. 1) Example input values: a) Gross Weight - 135,000 lb (61,235 kg) EFFECTIVITY ALL b) Brakes on Speed - 120 knots (222 km/h) (no wind) c) Pressure Altitude - 5000 ft (2 km) d) Outside Air Temperature - 80°F (27°C) e) Landing stop using maximum manual braking f) No Thrust Reversers. 2) Example result values: a) Resultant Brake Energy - 26,000,000 ft-lb (35,251,268 N·m) b) Resultant is in the COOLING RECOMMENDED range. (8) A high energy condition can be a refused takeoff. (a) It can also be any stop or sequence of stops that collect energy in the CAUTION or FUSE PLUG MELT range (Figure 202 or Figure 203). (9) An indication that a high energy stop, or equivalent, has occurred is the release of a wheel fuse plug. NOTE: If fuse plug releases do occur, the condition is a high energy stop within the fuse plug melt range. (a) Energy levels are different between brakes after stops in the COOLING RECOMMENDED range. (b) One or more brakes could have absorbed energy in the CAUTION range, and one or more wheel fuse plugs released. (10) For main landing gear tires that have been subjected to unusual service events, such as high energy rejected takeoffs, high energy stops, or high energy overspeed landings where thermal fuse plugs have melted, these tires should be removed and discarded. If the main landing gear tires on the airplane remain inflated, remove the wheel-tire assembly and send the hardware to your local wheel shop for the inspection. (a) Make sure to identify all tires of the unusual service event when returning the tires to the supplier. (11) If the nose and main landing gear tires exceed their respective tire speed rating during the overspeed landing, remove the wheel-tire assembly and send the hardware to your local wheel shop for inspection. (a) Make sure to identify all tires of the unusual service event when returning the tires to the supplier.

D. High Energy Stop Conditional Inspection - In CAUTION range

SUBTASK 05-51-07-210-001 (1) Do the steps that follow for the In Caution range inspection (Figure 204): (a) Move the airplane away from the runway. 1) Do not use the brakes very much when you move the airplane. 2) Do not set the parking brake. WARNING DO NOT GO NEAR THE MAIN LANDING GEAR FOR 1 HOUR AFTER THE AIRPLANE MAKES A HIGH-ENERGY STOP. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (b) Let the brakes, tires, and wheels cool so you can touch them. (c) Examine the tires, do this task: Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803. NOTE: Low tire pressure compared to the other tires can show a melted fuse plug. 1) If a fuse plug has melted, do the FUSE PLUG MELT Range inspection. (d) Examine the wheels, do this task: Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801. (e) Examine the brakes, do this task: Main Landing Gear Brake Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-41-41-700-802. (f) If the high energy condition was a refused takeoff do the step that follows: 1) Examine the thrust reverser blocker door cover assembly for cracking.

E. High Energy Stop Conditional Inspection - In FUSE PLUG MELT range or Brake Fire

SUBTASK 05-51-07-210-002 (1) Do the steps that follow for the In FUSE PLUG MELT range inspection (Figure 204): (a) Move the airplane away from the runway immediately because the tires will possibly deflate. (b) Do not set the parking brake. (c) Do not let the airplane move, do one of these steps: 1) Keep the tow tug connected to the airplane. 2) Put the chocks on the nose landing gear tires (CHOCK INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING DO NOT GO NEAR THE MAIN LANDING GEAR FOR 1 HOUR AFTER THE AIRPLANE MAKES A HIGH-ENERGY STOP. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT SPRAY EXTINGUISHER OR COOLANT DIRECTLY ON THE INFLATED TIRE OR WHEEL. AN EXPLOSION CAN OCCUR. IT CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (d) Decrease the temperature of the wheel or tire, do one of these steps: NOTE: A different source of cooling can be an air conditioning cart or truck. 1) After 1 hour, use water mist or fog on the wheel or tire to decrease the temperature. 2) Wait 2 to 3 hours for the brakes, wheels and tires to cool until they can be touched. 3) If a chemical agent is used to extinguish a brake-area fire, do these steps: a) Wait until brakes and adjacent components are cool. b) Fully clean the extinguishing agent from the brakes and adjacent components. c) Use a large quantity of low pressure and clean water to clean the brakes (TASK 05-51-95-100-801). (e) Examine the tires on the axles where all tires are inflated, do this task: Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803. (f) Examine the wheels on the axles where all tires are inflated, do this task: Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801. (g) Examine the brakes on the axles where all tires are inflated, do this task: Main Landing Gear Brake Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-41-41-700-802. (h) Remove all main gear tires and wheels on the axles where at least one tire was deflated, do this task: Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Removal, TASK 32-45-11-000-801. NOTE: Do this step after the landing gear is cool and safe to go near. (i) Discard the tires from the wheels with melted fuse plugs. (j) For wheels with good fuse plugs do these steps: 1) Remove the wheel-tire assembly from service. NOTE: Your preferred wheel shop or wheel repair facility will disassemble and examine the hardware to make sure it is serviceable. 2) Tag the wheel-tire assembly with the reason for removal. (k) On the axles where at least one tire was deflated, look for seized or damaged brakes, do this task: Main Landing Gear Brake Check (Wheel Removed from the Airplane), TASK 32-41-41-700-803. (l) Remove the antiskid wheel speed transducer on the axles where at least one tire was deflated, do this task: Transducer Removal, TASK 32-42-11-000-801. (m) Remove the brakes on the axles where the tires are deflated and you found damaged brakes, do this task: Main Landing Gear Brake Removal, TASK 32-41-41-000-801. 1) If a dry chemical fire extinguisher was used to extinguish a landing gear brake fire, visually check for chemical residue. NOTE: Heat damage can cause cadmium embrittlement of the steel substrate and is not always found by non-destructive inspection procedures. NOTE: Send the parts to the shop for approved repairs. 4) If the inspection in the first step 1) above shows that the coating has melted, inspect for evidence of embrittlement or cracking. a) Use the fluorescent magnetic particle inspection techniques. (41 cm). 1) Look for discoloration or blistering. a) Green paint will change to a light brown or black color. b) Light gray paint will change to a yellow color. NOTE: Do not land the airplane more than three times before you do this inspection. (p) If the high energy condition was a refused takeoff do the step that follows: 1) Examine the thrust reverser blocker door cover assembly for cracking.

05-51-07-280-801Heat Damage Inspection (Ammonium Persulfate Solution)PDF p. 878

3. Heat Damage Inspection (Ammonium Persulfate Solution)

A. General

(1) This inspection is used to find if the high strength steel that showed visible signs of heat damage, had changed. (a) It will look for a change in the temper or heat treat properties. NOTE: Refer to product Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) and local requirements for proper handling procedures. (2) This inspection will usually occur on the components of the landing gear axles. (a) The signs of discolored or blistered paint or plating shows that a general intense heat has changed the temper of the axle. 1) When this happens, the ammonium persulfate procedure should be applied to the damaged part of the axle.

B. References

E. Ammonium Persulfate Solution Procedure

SUBTASK 05-51-07-120-001 (1) Do the steps that follow to apply the solution, ammonium persulfate compound, G02412. NOTE: 100 grams of ammonium persulfate per 0.27 gal (1.02 l) of tap water will make the necessary solution. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING DO NOT BREATHE THE VAPORS OF THE CAUSTIC STRIPPER. DO NOT GET IT IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (a) Remove the paint from the heat damage areas. (b) Strip the cadmium surface with sandpaper, abrasive cloth, B00102 applied by hand. 1) Strip a minimum area of 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) larger than the area that is to be tested. WARNING DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES OF THE SOLVENTS OR ETCH SOLUTIONS. DO NOT GET THEM IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (c) Clean the area to be etched, with an applicable solvent like solvent, B00081. (d) Remove the cadmium plating. (e) Apply the ammonium persulfate solution, with a cheesecloth, cotton wiper, G00034, on the surface to be tested for 30 to 60 seconds. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE ETCHANT SOLUTION DOES NOT TOUCH THE CADMIUM PLATED SURFACES. POISONOUS FUMES CAN OCCUR. IT CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL. (f) Rinse the surface with hot or cold water immediately. NOTE: Alcohol can also be used. (g) Dry the surface with clean, dry compressed air, immediately.

F. Examine the Etched Area.

SUBTASK 05-51-07-210-003 (1) Do the steps that follow to examine the etched areas: (a) Examine the parts with a bright light and without magnification. 1) Look for signs of heat damage. (b) If all of the etched area is the same shade of gray, there was no change to the temper of the steel. (c) If the area has been too hot it will be a lighter or darker color than the normal color. NOTE: Darker color shows over-tempered martensite. NOTE: Darker color in a lighter circle shows untempered martensite surrounded by overtempered material. (d) If the etched area is mottled (has spots or streaks of a different color), the condition of the heat treat will be unknown. NOTE: If this condition occurs, replace the axle. 1) Replace the axle if it is necessary, do this task: Main Landing Gear Axle Removal, TASK 32-11-85-000-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL

G. Put the airplane back to its usual condition.

SUBTASK 05-51-07-120-002 (1) Remove the etch with applicable abrasive paper, abrasive cloth, B00102. NOTE: Do this step if the part is serviceable. NOTE: If it is not serviceable, install replacement parts. (2) Stylus the cadmium plate areas where the plating was removed (SOPM 20-42-10). SUBTASK 05-51-07-370-001 (3) Refinish the surface with the correct primer and paint, do this task: Prepare the Surface to be Painted, TASK 51-21-21-370-801. SUBTASK 05-51-07-400-001 (4) Install the axle if it is applicable, do this task: Main Landing Gear Axle Installation, TASK 32-11-85-420-801. SUBTASK 05-51-07-400-002 (5) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Brake Installation, TASK 32-41-41-400-801. SUBTASK 05-51-07-400-003 (6) Do this task: Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit Installation, TASK 32-42-21-400-801. SUBTASK 05-51-07-400-004 (7) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Installation, TASK 32-45-11-400-801.

A. General

(1) If the tires have been subjected to an overspeed landing above the rated tire speed, all tires on the airplane should be removed and discarded.

SUBTASK 05-51-07-020-001 (1) If the tires have been subjected to an overspeed landing above the rated tire speed, do these steps: (a) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Removal, TASK 32-45-11-000-801. (b) Do this task: Nose Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly - Removal, TASK 32-45-21-000-801. (c) Discard all tires after removing them from the airplane.

2. Phase I Inspection

A. Airplane Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-09-212-003 (1) Do the inspection of the main and nose landing gear. (a) Examine all tires and wheels. (b) Examine the support structure. (c) Look for signs of fluid leakage at the top and bottom of the outer cylinder of the shock strut. NOTE: A small quantity of hydraulic fluid on the surface of the inner cylinder of the shock strut is satisfactory. SUBTASK 05-51-09-212-004 (2) Do the inspection of the landing gear, fuselage, and wing. (a) Look for fuel leaks, and other fluid leaks, in the areas that follow: 1) All wheel well areas of the body, wing, and nose landing gear. 2) The lower external surface of the fuselage in the area of the wing-to-body fairing. 3) The wing.

B. Airplane Inspection

SUBTASK 05-51-09-212-005 (1) Do the inspection of the main landing gear and support structure. (a) Make sure the shock strut pressures are normal and the hydraulic fluids are at the correct levels MAIN LANDING GEAR SHOCK STRUT - SERVICING, PAGEBLOCK 12-15-31/301. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Lift the airplane with jacks Lift the Airplane with the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-815. (c) Examine the inner and outer cylinder lugs. (d) Examine all structural components of the main landing gear and carefully examine the components that follow: 1) Shock strut 2) Trunnion Link 3) Drag strut 4) Torsion links 5) Side strut 6) Walking beam fitting of the shock strut 7) Walking beam for the main gear actuator 8) Linkage fittings of the walking beam and actuator 9) The attach nut of the orifice support tube (signs of fluid leakage) 10) Strut doors and the mechanism that retracts and extends the doors (e) Examine the support structure of the main landing gear and carefully examine the components that follow: 1) Landing gear beam 2) Support fittings for the landing gear beam: a) Inboard b) Outboard. 3) Trunnion support fittings and attachment: a) Forward b) Aft 4) Stabilizer link and fittings between the rear spar and landing gear beam 5) Body fitting for side strut and uplock attachment (f) Examine all of the pin joints and fuse pin connections. (g) If you found tire damage in Phase 1, do the steps that follow. 1) Remove and examine the wheel structure. 2) Remove and examine the brake assembly. 3) Examine the axles. (h) If one or more of the conditions that follow occurred; remove, disassemble, and examine all parts of the shock strut MAIN LANDING GEAR - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 32-11-00/401. 1) The shock strut pressures were sufficiently low to cause damage. 2) They hydraulic fluid levels were sufficiently low to cause damage. 3) You found damage to one or more of the parts during your inspection of the landing gear. NOTE: Do not remove the orifice support tube to examine it. (i) Make sure the main landing gear retracts and extends correctly MAIN GEAR EXTENSION AND RETRACTION - ADJUSTMENT/TEST, PAGEBLOCK 32-32-00/501. EFFECTIVITY ALL (j) Lower the airplane from the jacks Lower the Airplane Off the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-816 SUBTASK 05-51-09-212-006 (2) Do the inspection of the nose landing gear and support structure. (a) Make sure the shock strut pressures are normal and the hydraulic fluids are at the correct levels NOSE LANDING GEAR SHOCK STRUT - SERVICING, PAGEBLOCK 12-15-41/301. (b) Lift the nose of the airplane with jacks Lift the Airplane Nose with the Nose Jack at Jack Point D, TASK 07-11-21-580-801. (c) If you found tire damage in Phase 1, do the steps that follow. 1) Remove and examine the wheel structure 2) Examine the axle (d) Examine all structural components of the nose landing gear and carefully examine the components that follow: 1) Shock strut 2) Torsion links 3) Drag strut 4) Lock links 5) Drag brace link 6) The attach nut of the orifice support tube (signs of fluid leakage) (e) Examine the wheel well area and carefully examine the parts that follow: 1) Web (the left and right sidewalls) 2) Aft bulkhead 3) Trunnion attachments 4) Drag strut attachments (f) Examine the wheel well bulkheads and fuselage outboard of nose wheel well at (Body Stations 294.5 and 360). NOTE: You can do this inspection on the forward side through the access holes in the sidewalls of the nose wheel well. Examine the aft side of the bulkhead at Body Station 294.5 from the electronics compartment. (g) If one or more of the conditions that follow occurred remove, disassemble, and examine all parts of the shock strut NOSE LANDING GEAR - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 32-21-00/401. 1) The shock strut pressures were sufficiently low to cause damage. 2) The hydraulic fluid levels were sufficiently low to cause damage. 3) You found damage to one or more of the parts during your inspection of the landing gear. NOTE: Do not remove the orifice support tube to examine it. (h) Make sure the nose landing gear steering system is adjusted and operates correctly NOSE WHEEL STEERING SYSTEM - ADJUSTMENT/TEST, PAGEBLOCK 32-51-00/501. (i) Make sure the nose landing gear retracts and extends correctly NOSE GEAR EXTENSION AND RETRACTION - ADJUSTMENT/TEST, PAGEBLOCK 32-33-00/501. EFFECTIVITY ALL (j) Lower the nose of the airplane from the jacks Lower the Airplane Nose Off of the Jack, TASK 07-11-21-580-802. SUBTASK 05-51-09-212-007 (3) Do the inspection of the fuselage. NOTE: If you find external damage to the fuselage, always examine the adjacent internal structure. (a) Examine the lower fuselage structure. NOTE: Examine carefully in the area below the body crease from Body Station 727 to 100 inches (254cm) aft. (b) Examine carefully these components (Body Stations 540 through 727A): 1) Keel beam chords 2) Stiffeners 3) Webs and splices (c) Also examine carefully the top of the fuselage between S-6 left and S-6 right (Body Stations 540, 664, 727). (d) Examine the upper and lower fuselage skin panels forward and aft of the wing. NOTE: Permanent wrinkles frequently occur on the lower side of the fuselage skins aft of Body Station 727. An internal inspection is necessary if you found wrinkles that were not there before the landing. Examine the wrinkles carefully for cracks. (e) Examine the wing-to-fuselage joints (Body Stations 540 and 664). (f) Examine the fuselage skin joints above the landing gear beam.

C. Put the Airplane Back to its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 05-51-09-430-001 (1) Install the components you removed or install replacement components.

05-51-12-110-801Toilet Over-Servicing Condition - CleaningPDF p. 911

2. Toilet Over-Servicing Condition - Cleaning

A. General

(1) If blue water contamination is found in the airplane, after an over-servicing event has occurred, an immediate cleanup action is necessary to prevent possible contamination of electrical or electronic components. (2) It is possible for blue water contamination to occur in a single isolated area or more than one area, dependent upon the amount of liquid spilled. All contaminated areas are to be completely cleaned. (3) It is most important that all moisture is removed from the contaminated area. Clean cloths and dry air are to be used. (4) In all areas where blue water contamination has to be removed and cleaned, you must use an approved disinfectant to kill all harmful micro-organisms. (5) The flight safety of the airplane, together with the safety of health and the prevention of bad smells, must be your first consideration when you complete this task.

B. References

Reference Title 12-17-01-610-801 Waste Tank Servicing (P/B 301) 20-30-31 P/B 201 CLEANERS AND POLISHES - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES 38-32-01-400-801-001 Toilet Shroud Installation (P/B 401) 38-32-01-400-843-003 Toilet Shroud Installation (P/B 401)

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification G00034 Cotton Wiper - Process Cleaning Absorbent Wiper (Cheesecloth, Gauze) AMS3819 Class 1 Grade A or B Form 1 (Supersede BMS15-5 CL A) G50316 Cloth - Clean, Dry, Lint-free, White, Cotton

D. Access Panels

Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door 117BL Forward Airstair Door EFFECTIVITY ALL

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 05-51-12-110-002 WARNING ALWAYS PUT ON RUBBER GLOVES BEFORE YOU DO MAINTENANCE ON THE TOILET SYSTEM, OR TOUCH PARTS THAT TOUCHED WASTE MATERIAL. FULLY CLEAN YOUR HANDS WITH SOAP AND WATER AFTER MAINTENANCE IS COMPLETED. THE TOILET WASTE CAN CAUSE ILLNESS AND INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (1) Put on protective clothing before you begin to clean up the blue water. (2) Use a clean cotton cloth, G50316 or cotton wiper, G00034 to remove the blue water from the contamination area. NOTE: If a large quantity of liquid is to be removed, a suction pump should be used to drain the contaminated area. (3) Use approved cleaning agents and disinfectants when you clean areas where blue water contamination has occurred, CLEANERS AND POLISHES - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES, PAGEBLOCK 20-30-31/201. (4) When blue water is found in the lavatory area, do the steps that follow: (a) Remove laying blue water from all surfaces. NOTE: Most of the blue water should drain out of the airplane through the floor drains and the waste water system. 1) Use clean fresh water to dilute contaminated areas of the blue stain. (b) If there are signs of blue water on the toilet tank, make sure you remove all blue water stains from the toilet tank and all related components and connections. NOTE: It is important that all blue stains are removed from the area. This will allow accurate visual inspections to be done in the future. (c) If blue water was found on the modular toilet, make sure all signs of blue water stains are removed and the weep holes in the floor pan are free from blockage. (d) Use a clean, moisture-free cotton cloth, G50316 or cotton wiper, G00034 to fully dry all surfaces and components. (e) Use a dry air supply to fully remove additional moisture from the contaminated areas which are difficult to touch. (f) If there are surface areas which remain with a blue stain, make a record of the precise location. NOTE: A record of a blue stain area can help to find the cause of a possible new leak of blue water, should a leak occur in the future. (5) If blue water is found in the electronic equipment compartment, do the steps that follow: (a) Protect adjacent areas to the contaminated area, from the cleaning procedure, by the use of polyethylene sheeting as a waterproof cover. (b) Use clean fresh water to dilute contaminated areas of the blue stain. (c) Use a clean cotton cloth, G50316 or cotton wiper, G00034 to remove laying blue water from all areas shown during the toilet over-servicing inspection of the electronic equipment compartment. (d) If the airstair drip pan is contaminated by blue water, do the steps that follow: 1) Make sure the airstair drip pan is drained of liquid. EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117BL Forward Airstair Door 3) Fully clean the airstair drip pan and access panel with fresh water. 4) Make sure the drain in the access panel is free from blockage. (e) Use a clean cloth to fully dry all surfaces and use a dry air supply to dry the areas which are difficult to touch. (f) If the area below the toilet tank shows signs of blue water contamination, fully clean the drain tube, the ground flush hose or the drain valve control cable with fresh water. NOTE: You must be most careful with the use of water in the electronic equipment compartment; additional contamination must not occur. (g) If the blue water contamination shows on the electronic racks and equipment, do the steps that follow: 1) Remove blue water from all surfaces, cables and connectors. 2) Use a dry air supply to remove all moisture from the contaminated areas. NOTE: Electrical cable looms can hold moisture between the separate wires. If possible, open the wires in a contaminated cable when you dry the cable. 3) Remove all signs of blue water from tubes which could conduct moisture, such as the pitot-static tubes, as necessary. 4) Do a check of contaminated connectors for blue water ingress and dry as necessary. NOTE: If you think a connector is contaminated with blue water, you must disconnect and fully examine the connector and the related equipment connector. (h) Do an operational test of equipment which possibly could have been contaminated with blue water. (6) Do the servicing procedure for the system Waste Tank Servicing, TASK 12-17-01-610-801. SUBTASK 05-51-12-840-002 (7) Return the aircraft to normal. (a) Remove warning placard from flight compartment. (b) Do a check of all hose connections and tighten connector clamps as necessary. (c) Close these access panels: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door 117BL Forward Airstair Door (d) Do this task: Toilet Shroud Installation, TASK 38-32-01-400-801-001 or Toilet Shroud Installation, TASK 38-32-01-400-843-003. (e) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: Power Distribution Panel Number 1, P91 Row Col Number Name C 11 C01388 VACUUM WASTE CONT F 2 C01389 VACUUM WASTE BLOWER EFFECTIVITY ALL (f) Remove all tools and equipment from the work area.

05-51-12-200-801Toilet Over-Servicing Condition - InspectionPDF p. 915

2. Toilet Over-Servicing Condition - Inspection

A. General

(1) This inspection procedure is to be done when an over-service of the toilet system has occurred or you think it has occurred. NOTE: The term "over-service" is used to show that too much blue water has been used during the servicing of the toilet system, and has spilled inside the airplane. (2) It is possible for blue water contamination to occur in a single isolated area or more than one area, dependent upon the amount of liquid spilled. (3) A full visual inspection is necessary to confirm the extent of possible blue water contamination. NOTE: Spilled liquid can use different flowpaths to disperse. (4) It is recommended to do a check of the airplane records to see if there has been a spill of blue water before and if blue stains remain. NOTE: Unnecessary work can be avoided if knowledge of another over-servicing is available for comparison.

B. References

NOTE: Drain the system only, do not complete a full service of the toilet system. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 05-51-12-040-001 (2) Deactivate the lavatory, do this task: Toilet Deactivation, TASK 38-32-00-040-801. SUBTASK 05-51-12-010-001 (3) Gain access to the lavatory in question. (a) Remove the lavatory shroud, do this task: Toilet Shroud Removal, TASK 38-32-01-000-801-001 or Toilet Shroud Removal, TASK 38-32-01-000-843-003. SUBTASK 05-51-12-210-001 (4) With the toilet shroud removed, do the inspection as follows: (a) Visually inspect the floor area around the toilet for any signs of blue water. (b) Visually inspect the area around the toilet tank for any signs of blue water. SUBTASK 05-51-12-010-002 (5) Extend the forward airstair for access, do this task: Forward Airstair Extension, TASK 52-61-00-860-801. SUBTASK 05-51-12-010-003 (6) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door Open the forward electronic bay for access. SUBTASK 05-51-12-210-002 (7) In the electronic equipment compartment, do a visual inspection as follows: (a) Look for signs of blue water in the area below the toilet tank. (b) Examine the toilet tank drain tube, the drain valve control cable, and ground flush hose for signs of blue water. (c) Examine the toilet drain floor adapter and the adjacent area for signs of blue water. (d) Examine the airstair drain pan and moisture shroud for signs of blue water. (e) If you find blue water has flowed into the electronic equipment compartment, put a warning placard in the flight compartment to tell all personal, "DO NOT OPERATE ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT", before you continue. NOTE: The blue water can use the outer surface of tubes and cables as flowpaths to contaminate different areas of the electronic equipment compartment. (f) If you find signs of blue water contamination in the electronic equipment compartment, do a full visual inspection of the compartment. NOTE: If a serious over-servicing occurs, it is possible for blue water to find flowpaths to many possible locations. (g) You must do full inspections of all electrical cable looms for signs of blue water. (h) You must do an inspection of all tubes, such as the pitot-static tubes, for signs of blue water. SUBTASK 05-51-12-110-001 (8) If you find any evidence that blue water has spilled, do this task: Toilet Over-Servicing Condition - Cleaning, TASK 05-51-12-110-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 05-51-12-840-001 (9) If you find no evidence of blue water spillage or have already performed Toilet Over-Servicing Condition - Cleaning, TASK 05-51-12-110-801, then do the following to return the aircraft to normal. (a) Do this task: Forward Airstair Retraction, TASK 52-61-00-860-802. (b) Do this task: Toilet Shroud Installation, TASK 38-32-01-400-801-001 or Toilet Shroud Installation, TASK 38-32-01-400-843-003. (c) Complete the servicing portion of Waste Tank Servicing, TASK 12-17-01-610-801. (d) Install all components and access panels removed for the inspection.

05-51-13-211-801Galley Spill Conditional - InspectionPDF p. 919

2. Galley Spill Conditional - Inspection

A. General

(1) This inspection procedure is to be done when liquid has been spilled in the galley area. NOTE: When a small amount of liquid is spilled, an inspection is not usually necessary. (2) In the galley areas, a water (liquid) barrier is installed to contain liquid when it is spilled. To protect the water barrier, vinyl mats cover the galley floor. (3) In the adjacent entry and service door thresholds, waste water drains are installed to remove liquids (gray water) from the floor. These drain holes must be kept free from blockages. (4) The integrity of the water barrier seal, in the forward galley areas, is most important because the location of the electronic equipment compartment is directly below the forward galley. (5) A leak from the forward galley which has a damaged water barrier, into the compartment below, could possibly cause serious damage to the electronic equipment. The result could be a possible hazard to the flight safety of the airplane. (6) In all areas where gray water contamination has to be removed and cleaned, you must use an approved disinfectant to kill all harmful micro-organisms. (7) The flight safety of the airplane, together with the safety of health and the prevention of bad smells, must be your first consideration when you do this task.
